problem: "The project is ₹5,000 ahead of the spending line" describes an overspend as if it were good progress. Spending ₹29,000 when the plan says ₹24,000 means ₹5,000 more money has gone out than planned; a student will read "ahead" as "doing well" and miss that this is a cost overrun.
fix: "If actual spend is ₹29,000, the project is ₹5,000 over the planned spending line — a cost overrun, not progress. Spending above plan only looks acceptable if the work finished is also ahead; here the manager must check scope or cost."

problem: The formula B × k ÷ N silently assumes money is spent at the same rate every week. Real projects spend unevenly (design and testing weeks cost more), so the flat ₹4,000 per week is an assumption that is never stated.
fix: Add one line: "This assumes an even spend across weeks; if spend is uneven, add the weekly planned amounts up to week k instead."
